# Results — Study 738 (Pollen-Season)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: **the
owners of the big allergy brands carry a repeatable spring seasonal** — US hay-fever
season (tree/grass pollen, ~March→May) drives an antihistamine/nasal-spray demand spike,
so a basket of the listed brand owners should beat the market through the pollen window.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the 2026 spring window
closed 2026-05-30, so 2026 is a complete event). Fingerprints `09ea36482502` (BAYRY) /
`063cf5d088aa` (SNY) / `f10b7c3e080d` (PRGO) / `5f77bcceb9b7` (KVUE) / `b95efb29b67e`
(HLN) / `6685430bd981` (SPY) / `2d7f448f48d3` (XLP).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`): BAYRY 7,449 rows (from 1996-11), SNY 6,038 (2002-07), PRGO 7,673 (1996-01), KVUE 791 (2023-05), HLN 987 (2022-07); benchmarks SPY 7,673 (1996-01) and XLP 6,921 (1998-12) — all sliced ≤ 2026-06-30 |
| Pollen window | a **labelled, cited calendar rule** (not a data feed): last session of February → last session on/before May 31 — US spring tree/grass pollen, AAFA "Allergy Capitals" / AAAAI regional pollen calendars. Fixed dates known years ahead ⇒ **calendar-known, no execution lag** |
| Basket | 5 listed owners of household allergy brands: **BAYRY** (Claritin), **SNY** (Allegra/Dupixent), **PRGO** (private-label OTC), **KVUE** (Zyrtec/Benadryl), **HLN** (Flonase) — equal-weighted each year over whichever names cover the full window |
| Events | **30 independent, non-overlapping spring windows, 1997 → 2026.** Coverage **named, never back-filled**: 2 names (BAYRY/PRGO) pre-2003, 3 (+SNY) to 2022, 4 in 2023 (Kenvue not yet listed at the February entry), 5 from 2024 |
| Statistics | One-sample *t* across the 30 yearly abnormal returns (the correct unit — independent events, **not** a daily panel); Wilson interval on the hit rate; block-bootstrap CI on the mean; 20-seed × 250-draw random-window placebo |
| Execution / costs | the window is calendar-known (no lag). The timer goes **long basket / short SPY** at the February entry close, exits at the end-May close; both legs charged one-way × NAV (5/10 bps), the short SPY leg pays **borrow** (50 bps annual ≈ 12.6 bps over the ~63-session window) |
| Survivorship (named) | the basket holds only *currently-listed* owners; two are recent spin-offs (Kenvue 2023, Haleon 2022) that enter only post-listing. A 3-name full-history core basket (BAYRY/SNY/PRGO) cross-checks that the spin-offs don't drive the result |

Total-return (dividends reinvested) throughout — the honest comparison for equities;
never a price-only series under a total-return banner.

## The headline — basket minus market over the pollen window

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean abnormal return (basket − SPY) | **+2.03%** |
| one-sample *t* (n=30) | **+1.06** |
| sd across years | 10.47% |
| hit rate (basket beat the market) | **19/30 = 63.3%** (Wilson 95% [45.5%, 78.1%]) |
| block-bootstrap 95% CI on the mean | **[−1.71%, +5.63%]** |

The basket beats the market by an average **+2.03%** through the pollen window, and does
so in **63%** of years — the sign the folklore predicts. But the one-sample *t* is
**+1.06**, nowhere near the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar; the hit-rate's Wilson interval
comfortably includes 50%; and the bootstrap CI on the mean **straddles zero** by a wide
margin. Positive-leaning, yes — statistically certifiable, no.

## The random-window placebo — and why it disagrees (a teaching case)

Same-length windows drawn at random *non-spring* anchor dates, 20 seeds × 250 draws.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spring mean | +203.0 bps |
| placebo mean (random windows) | **−107.0 bps** |
| placebo sd | 182.2 bps |
| right-tail *p* | **0.048** |

At face value this is borderline "significant" (*p* = 0.048). **It disagrees with the
one-sample *t* = 1.06 because the two tests null different things.** The one-sample *t*
asks *"did the basket make money, market-adjusted, in spring?"* (answer: not
distinguishably — +2.03%, *t* = 1.06). The placebo asks *"is spring special versus a
random window?"* — and it is, but **only because the basket structurally bleeds vs the
market the rest of the year** (a random window averages **−107 bps**). Spring merely
looks special against that negative baseline. The honest reading is the vs-**zero** test,
which the effect fails; the placebo's borderline *p* is a single cut riding entirely on
the basket's own drag, not evidence of a bankable spring edge.

## Robustness — a fairer benchmark and the spin-off-free core basket

| cut | mean abnormal | one-sample *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| basket − SPY (headline) | +2.03% | **+1.06** | 30 |
| basket − XLP (consumer staples) | +3.58% | **+1.65** | 28 |
| 3-name core (BAYRY/SNY/PRGO) − SPY | +2.02% | **+1.06** | 30 |

The strongest cut is against consumer staples (*t* = 1.65) — still short of the bar. The
3-name full-history core basket reproduces the headline almost exactly, so the two recent
spin-offs (Kenvue, Haleon) are **not** manufacturing the result. No cut clears |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Calendar-month seasonality — a blunt cross-check

Mean daily abnormal return (basket − SPY) by calendar month, 1997→2026 (a coarse read;
the window test is primary).

| month | J | F | **M** | **A** | **M** | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean (bps/day) | +0.7 | −4.6 | **+2.9** | **+4.1** | **−1.4** | −0.5 | −3.7 | −6.8 | +4.1 | −9.3 | −4.5 | +4.4 |
| *t* | +0.1 | −0.8 | **+0.6** | **+0.7** | **−0.3** | −0.1 | −0.7 | −1.3 | +0.8 | −1.6 | −0.8 | +0.9 |

March and April lean mildly positive (+2.9 / +4.1 bps/day) — but so do September and
December, and no month clears |*t*| ≥ 2. There is no clean "spring lights up, the other
months don't" picture; the pollen months are inside the ordinary monthly noise.

## The timer — long basket / short SPY over the window

Enter at the February close, exit at the end-May close; both legs one-way × NAV, the
short SPY leg pays 50 bps annual borrow (~12.6 bps over the window).

| cost (per leg) | gross | *t* (gross) | net | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | +203.0 bps | +1.06 | +190.4 bps | +1.00 |
| 5 bps | +203.0 bps | +1.06 | +170.4 bps | +0.89 |
| 10 bps | +203.0 bps | +1.06 | +150.4 bps | +0.79 |

The seasonal long/short earns a gross **+2.03%/yr**, but at *t* = 1.06 it is
indistinguishable from zero *before* a cent of cost; net of realistic costs and the short
leg's borrow it fades to **+1.70%/yr** at *t* = 0.89. A +2% edge you cannot tell apart
from zero is not something you can size — there is no certifiable edge to charge costs
against.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired basket/market random-walk tapes (~30 years), TUNABLE planted spring
bump on the pollen sessions; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.07** (sd 1.09), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** (≈ the 5% expected by chance, no bias) |
| planted bump = +6.0% (seed 738) | **+4.56** |

The detector centers on zero under the null (a planted-nothing world crosses the bar only
at roughly the chance rate) and lights up sharply on a genuine planted seasonal. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Mean spring abnormal return **+2.03%**, one-sample *t* = **+1.06**;
  no cut clears |*t*| ≥ 2 (vs staples 1.65, core basket 1.06), the bootstrap CI
  **[−1.71%, +5.63%]** straddles zero, and the hit-rate Wilson interval [45.5%, 78.1%]
  includes a coin flip. The one borderline number (random-window placebo *p* = 0.048) is
  an artifact of the basket's structural underperformance outside spring, not a bankable
  seasonal — measured against zero, the effect is inside the noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-basket/short-SPY seasonal earns a gross +2.03%/yr
  but at *t* = 1.06 it is undistinguishable from zero before costs; net of costs and
  borrow it is +1.70%/yr at *t* = 0.89. Nothing to size.
- **A tradable spring seasonal? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The direction leans the folklore's way
  (positive mean, 63% hit rate, borderline placebo), but on 30 independent years nothing
  clears the desk bar. Suggestive, not certified — the honest verdict on a real,
  intuitive story that the tape simply won't confirm at this sample size.
